get.summary: List hosts with IP, groups, and optional stats
get.description: Retrieve a list of all hosts with their IP addresses and associated host groups. Use include=stats to add package update counts (updates_count, security_updates_count, total_packages) to each host. Requires Basic Auth with scoped credentials (host:get permission).

parameters.name: hostgroup
parameters.description: Filter by host group name(s) or UUID(s). Comma-separated.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated. Supported: stats (adds updates_count, security_updates_count, total_packages, needs_reboot, os_type, os_version, last_update, status, effective_status, reporting_state, update_state). status is the stored provisioning lifecycle value, 'pending' before the first check-in and 'active' after it; it never becomes 'inactive'. effective_status is the value the web UI displays and is one of 'pending' | 'active' | 'inactive', where 'inactive' means an active host has not reported for more than twice the configured update interval. reporting_state is one of 'reporting' | 'overdue' | 'stale'. update_state is one of 'up_to_date' | 'updates_pending' | 'security_required'.

post.description: Agent heartbeat / ping. Requires X-API-ID and X-API-KEY. The body is optional; an empty body is accepted as a plain heartbeat. Every successful response carries hostId, the ID of the host these credentials belong to, so the agent can record it in config.yml as host_id.

hostId.description: host_id from the agent's config.yml (agent 2.1.4 or later). Ignored unless it is 1 to 64 letters, digits or hyphens. When it differs from the authenticated host's ID the ping still succeeds, the response sets hostIdMismatch, and the host is flagged with a host ID mismatch.

configVersion.description: config_version from the agent's config.yml (agent 2.1.4 or later). Stored only when it starts with N.N.N, optionally followed by a pre-release or build suffix, and is at most 64 bytes; anything else is ignored.

machineId.description: Machine ID of the host (agent 2.1.4 or later). Used with the hostname hash to detect two machines reporting with the same credentials (a possible clone).

hostId.description: ID of the host the credentials belong to. Returned on every successful ping, including an empty-body heartbeat.

hostIdMismatch.description: Present and true only when the request carried a hostId that differs from hostId.

post.description: Trigger or report agent update. Requires X-API-ID and X-API-KEY. The response carries hostId, the ID of the host these credentials belong to.

example.error: Script type required as query parameter (e.g., ?type=proxmox-lxc or ?type=direct-host)

post.description:
Enroll a new host, or re-issue credentials for a host this token created that has never reported. Requires X-Auto-Enrollment-Key and X-Auto-Enrollment-Secret headers.

Without host_id, a new host is created (201), unless a host with the same machine_id and name exists (409, code machine_id_match). With host_id, the server looks the host up: if it is not found, a new host is created as usual; if it exists, has never reported or connected, was created by this same token and was enrolled with the same machine_id, a new API key is issued for it (200, reenrolled true; the API ID is kept). Otherwise the request is refused with a coded 409 or 429 and nothing is created. The token's max_hosts_per_day limit applies only when a host is created; a re-issue neither counts towards it nor is blocked by it. Every error response from the host_id path carries a machine-readable code.

host_id.description: Optional. The host_id from the machine's existing config.yml, if it has one. Must be 1 to 64 letters, digits or hyphens. It is never used as the ID of a new host.

200.description: Credentials re-issued for the existing host named by host_id. Same shape as 201 plus reenrolled: true. The host keeps its ID and API ID; only the API key is new.

400.description: Bad Request, for example a missing friendly_name or a host_id that is not 1 to 64 letters, digits or hyphens

example.error: IP address not authorized for this token

409.description: Conflict. Nothing is created and no credentials are issued. code is one of: host_reporting (the host named by host_id has already reported or its agent has connected, so it is never re-keyed by enrolment; usually a cloned machine, or credentials regenerated in the UI but not applied), host_not_reenrollable (the host was not created by this token, for example it was added in the UI, or the machine_id differs from the one it was enrolled with), machine_id_match (no host_id was sent and a host with the same machine_id and name already exists). The host_id path also returns host_id, and friendly_name only when this token created the host.

value.error: This host is already reporting to PatchMon. If its agent is broken, reinstall it with the install command on the host's page, or regenerate its credentials.
This host was added to PatchMon another way and cannot be re-enrolled with this token. Use the install command on the host's page.

429.description: Too Many Requests. Either credentials for the host named by host_id were re-issued less than 60 seconds ago (code reenrol_cooldown), or the token's max_hosts_per_day limit has been reached for a request that would create a host.

value.error: Credentials for this host were re-issued less than a minute ago. Try again shortly.

value.message: Maximum hosts per day allowed for this token

post.description: Clears the possible-clone flag on a host. The flag is set when two different machines appear to report with the same host credentials. Dismissing it does not change the credentials; if the machines keep alternating, the flag is set again. Regenerating the host's credentials also clears it. Requires a signed-in user with the can_manage_hosts permission.
